game.gwt.name: Great Western Trail
game.gwt.description: You are ranchers driving cattle from Texas to Kansas City, then shipping them west by train. Each loop around the trail you hire cowboys, craftsmen, and engineers, put up buildings, and chase a stronger herd. When the job market fills, everyone scores the same categories as the official First Edition pad.
game.gwt2.name: Great Western Trail Second Edition
game.gwt2.description: Wrangle your herd of cows across the prairie and deliver it to Kansas City. Second Edition adds solo play, new art by Chris Quilliams, Simmental cattle, extra buildings, exchange tokens, and new station master tiles.
game.gwt2.stationMastersHelper: Score each station master in front of you. These tasks are independent of objective cards: 1 VP per worker in your worker section (including printed); 3 VP per 2 objective cards in your area (fulfilled or not); 3 VP per 2 hazards; 3 VP per green+orange outlaw pair; 3 VP per 2 certificates; 3 VP per 2 station discs; 2 VP per private building on the board.
game.gwta.name: Great Western Trail Argentina
game.gwta.description: Travel the plains of the Pampas with your cattle and deliver them to Buenos Aires. Argentina adds ships, city maps, farmer tiles, exhaustion cards, and new station master tiles.
game.gwta.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points. Tap the 2-VP disc and job market token rows to toggle them.
game.gwta.coinsHelper: Enter cash. Every 5 pesos becomes 1 victory point. Leftover pesos do not score.
game.gwta.shipsHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs on the ships. Negative VP are subtracted. The total can be negative.
game.gwta.cityMapsHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs on the city maps. Most quays also score VP per disc.
game.gwta.stationsHelper: Sum the VP printed next to each train station that has your disc. Extra markers on the final station score that station again.
game.gwta.farmersHelper: 2 VP for each farmer tile in front of you. Do not count farmer tiles on your player board.
game.gwta.cattleHelper: From your draw stack, hand, and discard pile, add VP on exhaustion cards and cattle cards. Subtract any negative VP.
game.gwta.stationMastersHelper: Score each station master in front of you. These tasks are independent of objective cards: 3 VP per 2 discs left on ships; 3 VP per 2 objective cards in your area; 4 VP per set of gaucho, carpenter, engineer, and farmer; 1 VP per cattle card of breeding value 3–5; 3 VP per 2 station discs (last station once); 3 VP per 2 workers with a strength icon; 1 VP per farmer tile in front of you (not on your board); 1 VP per 2 private buildings on the board.
game.gwtnz.name: Great Western Trail New Zealand
game.gwtnz.description: Run a sheep station on the South Island of New Zealand. Breed better sheep, raise the value of your wool, and ship it from the harbours to trading posts around the world.
game.gwtnz.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points. Tap the 3-VP disc and bonus tiles token rows to toggle them.
game.gwtnz.coinsHelper: Enter cash. Every 5 pounds becomes 1 victory point. Leftover pounds do not score.
game.gwtnz.tradingPostsHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs on all trading post crests (local, foreign, and wool). Negative VP are subtracted. The total can be negative.
game.gwtnz.harboursHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs and storehouses on small and medium harbours of the sea routes board.
game.gwtnz.pathfinderHelper: Enter the VP unlocked by your disc on the pathfinder track (shown next to or below your disc, at the most recent unlocked VP space).
game.gwtnz.hazardsHelper: Sum the VP printed on the hazard tiles and bonus tiles in front of you. Negative VP are subtracted.
game.gwtnz.cattleHelper: From your draw stack, hand, and discard pile, add the VP on sheep cards and bonus cards (except bonus objective cards).
game.gwtnz.stationMastersHelper: Score each harbourmaster tile in front of you. These tasks are independent of objective cards: 1 VP per certificate (permanent or temporary); 1 VP per 2 storehouses on the sea routes board; 1 VP per objective card in your area (fulfilled or not); 1 VP per private building on the board; 1 VP per hazard tile; 1 VP per card in your deck showing a ferry (including Set 1 bonus cards); 2 VP per 5 spaces advanced on the pathfinder track; 1 VP per 2 worker tiles in your worker section (including printed ones).
game.gwtnz.playerBoardHelper: 4 VP for each worker on the 5th space of any worker row. Add 2 and/or 4 VP if you cleared the matching pair of storehouses on your player board.
gwt.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points. Tap the 3-VP disc and job market token rows to toggle them.
gwt.coinsHelper: Enter cash. Every 5 dollars becomes 1 victory point. Leftover dollars do not score.
gwt.randomizer.hint: Each private building uses side A or B. All players use the same sides.
gwt.randomizer.publicHint: Shuffle the {n} public buildings onto board spaces A–{last}. For a first game, place each tile on its matching letter.
gwt.bonusCards.hint: Draws 4 of the 10 bonus card sets. Stack them below the bonus cards tiles in set-number order: the lowest set below the steering wheel, then the barrel and the bell, and the highest below the compass.
gwt.startingResources.pathfinderNote: Then, on your first turn, move a disc from a white-cornered space on your player board onto space 0 of the pathfinder track.
gwt.startingCards.title: Starting Cards
gwt.startingCards.exhaustionNote: Each starting deck also contains 1 Exhaustion card. Shuffle it in before you draw.
gwt.startingResources.cardsNote: Draw the cards from your own shuffled player deck.
gwt.startingResources.discardNote: Players {list}: discard down to {limit} cards at the start of your first turn.
gwt.startingResources.exchangeTokenNote: Playing with this expansion? Each player also receives 1 exchange token.
gwt.buildingsHelper: Sum the VP printed on your private building tiles on the board.
gwt.deliveriesHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs on city crests. Kansas City discs are −6 each. The total can be negative.
gwt.stationsHelper: Sum the VP printed next to each train station that has your disc.
gwt.hazardsHelper: Sum the VP printed on hazard tiles in front of you.
gwt.cattleHelper: From your draw stack, hand, and discard pile, add the VP printed on cattle cards.
gwt.objectivesHint: Leftover deck cards: add or drop; unmet subtract
gwt.objectivesHelper: Objective cards still in your deck can be added to your area or removed from the game (no immediate action). Then score your area: fulfilled cards add their VP, incomplete cards subtract theirs. The total can be negative.
gwt.stationMastersHelper: Score the individual tasks on station master tiles in front of you. Those tasks are independent of objective cards.
gwt.playerBoardHelper: 4 VP for each worker on the 5th or 6th space of any worker row (max 24).
game.arnak.name: Lost Ruins of Arnak
game.arnak.description: Lead an expedition onto the uncharted island of Arnak. Equip your team, uncover artifacts and archaeological sites, overcome guardians, and piece together research that may reveal the Lost Temple. After five rounds, score the same categories as the official pad.
game.arnak.footnote: Highest total wins. If tied, the first to the Lost Temple wins. If no one reached it, highest Research wins.
arnak.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points.
arnak.researchHelper: Add the points for each research token from its row. A magnifying glass in the Lost Temple scores based on the order it arrived.
arnak.templeTilesHelper: Sum the points printed on each temple tile you collected.
arnak.idolsHelper: 3 points per idol, even if it is in a slot. Then add the points printed in any empty idol slots.
arnak.guardiansHelper: 5 points for each guardian you overcame, whether you used the boon or not.
arnak.cardsHelper: Sum the points in the lower-right corner of each item and artifact in your deck, hand, and play area.
arnak.fearHelper: Fear cards score −1 each. If you have fear tiles, they score −2 each. Enter the total as a negative number.
arnak.darkTabletsHint: Altar majorities minus the cost of used dark tablets
arnak.altars.title: Altars & Dark Tablets
arnak.altars.intro: Enter how many dark tablets each player placed on each altar (0–3). The player with the most tablets on an altar gains its points. Ties are friendly: every tied player gains them.
arnak.altars.supply: {used} of {total} dark tablets used · {emptied} supply spaces emptied · each used tablet scores {per}
arnak.altars.overSupply: That is more tablets than the supply holds ({total}). Check the counts.
arnak.altars.rulesTitle: Scoring dark tablets: the cost of ambition
arnak.altars.rule1: 1. Return unused tablets. Any dark tablets players have left at the end of the game go back to the supply. Each space holds as many tablets as there are players.
arnak.altars.rule2: 2. Score negative points. The rightmost empty space of the dark tablet supply sets how many points each used tablet costs. For example, if that space shows 3, players lose 3 points for each dark tablet they played on altars.
arnak.altars.rule3: 3. Score altars. For each altar, the player who placed the most dark tablets on it gains the points printed above it. If there is a tie, all tied players gain those points.
arnak.altars.tip: Tip: Invoking altars can cost you points, but it gives big advantages during play. To offset the losses, pay attention to who has the most tablets on each altar.
arnak.leadersHint: Playing with the Expedition Leaders? Pick a unique leader for each player.
arnak.draft.hint: Add players and pick their colors, then each player gets {n} different leaders to choose from. No leader is offered to two players.
arnak.lostTempleTitle: Who reached the Lost Temple first?
arnak.lostTempleMessage: {names} are tied. Choose who got to the Lost Temple first.
arnak.lostTempleNoneHint: Highest Research among the tied players wins. If those are tied too, they share the win.
arnak.startingDeck.title: Your Starting Deck (Base Game)
arnak.startingDeck.leadersNote: Playing with leaders from the expansions? Each leader has a different starting deck, so use the leader's setup instead.
arnak.startingDeck.body: Each player has their own deck, and all decks start the same. Your deck should have the 4 basic cards in your color, plus 2 Fear cards:
game.cobse.name: The Castles of Burgundy Special Edition
game.cobse.description: Settle estates in the Duchy of Burgundy. Across five phases you draft tiles, complete colored regions, sell goods, and climb the victory track. The Special Edition adds solo play and the expansion tiles.
cob.quickReference.hint: Tap the sheet to turn it over.
cob.quickReference.pinch: Pinch to zoom in and out.
cob.quickReference.drag: Drag on the sheet to magnify a detail.
cob.duchy.label: Duchy
cob.duchy.hint.base: Each player draws one random duchy and chooses a side. The five double-sided boards are numbered 1–10, and each board has four copies. Sides 1 and 2 are the beginner duchy.
cob.duchy.hint.firstGame: For a first game, every player takes the beginner duchy and the same number, 1 or 2. Place the starting castle on the center space numbered 6.
cob.duchy.hint.firstExpansion: Each player receives one random duchy numbered 11–18. These are four double-sided boards, with four copies of each.
cob.duchy.hint.championship: The 2013 and 2016 championship boards are the two sides of one duchy, numbered 19 and 20. The box has four copies.
cob.duchy.hint.specialEdition: The Special Edition duchy is numbered 21 and 22, with four copies. Each player chooses a side.
cob.duchy.hint.borderPosts: Each player receives one random duchy numbered 23–30. The border posts are on the player board, so this expansion can also be played with any other duchy.
cob.duchy.hint.team: Each team uses halves 31a and 32a. The other side, 31b and 32b, is the advanced team board.
cob.duchy.hint.solo: The solo game uses one duchy. Side 33 is for beginning players. Side 34 is the advanced side.
cob.startingResources.note: After you determine the starting player, hand out workers clockwise: 1, then 2, 3, and 4. Every player also receives 1 silver coin and 3 random goods tiles.
game.shelfie.name: Shelfie Stacker
game.shelfie.description: Build the best board game shelfie. Each round you draft dice and stack them in the columns of your Big Shelf, chasing tall columns and high top dice. Dice you cannot place go to the Shelf of Shame. After the last round, score the same rows as the official pad.
game.shelfie.footnote: Highest total wins. If tied, the player with the lowest-valued Character Card still in hand wins. If still tied, the tied players share the victory.
shelfie.padHint: Tap a cell and enter how many columns or dice you have. The pad works out the points.
shelfie.fiveTallHelper: Count the columns in your Big Shelf with exactly 5 dice. Each scores 6 points.
shelfie.fourTallHelper: Count the columns in your Big Shelf with exactly 4 dice. Each scores 3 points.
shelfie.threeTallHelper: Count the columns in your Big Shelf with exactly 3 dice. Each scores 1 point.
shelfie.pipsHelper: Add up the pips on the top-most die of each column in your Big Shelf.
shelfie.rewardsHelper: Add the points from any Reward Cards you earned, such as First to Claim and End of Game cards.
shelfie.shameHelper: Count the dice in your Shelf of Shame. Each one costs 2 points.
shelfie.tieTitle: Who has the lowest Character Card?
shelfie.tieMessage: {names} are tied. Choose who has the lowest-valued Character Card still in hand.
shelfie.tieSharedHint: The tied players share the victory, and must say "Shelfie Stacker Sidekick" ten times quickly.
